regions.summary: Lower Li River hills: Cili, Shimen (Hunan) and Hefeng (Hubei).

candidates.name: Cili
candidates.meaning: Cili county (慈利, "kind benefit"), a county since 598; seat Lingyang town on the Li River.
candidates.fit: 46% of the region's people, and the region holds 85% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; Cili is also the seat of the Tianmen commandery (263-282) and Lingyang county.
candidates.source_note: 慈利县，598-1911，湖南慈利县驻地零阳镇 (sources.md)

candidates.name: Shimen
candidates.meaning: "Stone gate": county on the Li River, named for a rock gorge gate.
candidates.fit: 32% of the region's people but the region holds only 58% of the county; Cili is more central.
candidates.source_note: article listed in sources.md for region 1

regions.notes: Zhangjiajie (region 2) and Cili neighbour each other; no clash. Hefeng (Hubei, 16%) is skipped; its old name Rongmei is thinly known (43 hits with 湖南).

regions.summary: Zhangjiajie city: Yongding district, Sangzhi, Wulingyuan, part of Cili.

candidates.name: Zhangjiajie
candidates.meaning: Prefecture-level city named after the Zhangjiajie scenic area (literally the Zhang family's boundary), the sandstone pillar landscape of Wulingyuan.
candidates.fit: Holds Yongding (45%), the city seat, plus Wulingyuan and Sangzhi; the region holds 65% of the city's prefecture.
candidates.recognisability: Famous worldwide for its pillars (Avatar mountains).
candidates.source_note: article listed in sources.md for region 2

candidates.name: Sangzhi
candidates.meaning: "Mulberry planting": county in the upper Li River basin with Tujia and Bai people.
candidates.fit: 40% of the region's people, 98% of the county held; Sangzhi county (1729) and Chong prefecture seated here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; known as a Red Army base.

regions.summary: Longshan, Laifeng and Xuan'en on the You River at the Hunan, Hubei and Chongqing corner.

candidates.name: Longshan
candidates.meaning: "Dragon mountain": county named in 1729 for the Longshan hill; earlier Youyang and Qianyang counties.
candidates.fit: 51% of the region's people, 99.8% of the county held; Laifeng (24%) and Xuan'en (12%) are the rest.

candidates.name: Youshui
candidates.meaning: "You water": the largest tributary of the Yuan River, a boundary river here between Hunan and Hubei.
candidates.fit: Runs through Longshan and Laifeng, the heart of the region, then on into region 4.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 80 hits with 湖南, top ones about this river.
candidates.source_note: 酉水，沅水水系最大支流...流经保靖、龙山

candidates.name: Liye
candidates.meaning: Town in Longshan whose well in the Qin Qianling fort gave 36,000 Qin bamboo slips.
candidates.fit: Only 3% of the region's people, but a distinct name known for the Qin slips.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; Liye Qin slips article; 676 hits with 湖南.
candidates.source_note: 里耶秦简是在湖南西部里耶镇出土的36000余枚...简

regions.notes: Laifeng and Xuan'en are Hubei counties; the region mixes three provinces so Longshan fits as the Hunan majority.

regions.summary: Yongshun, Huayuan, Baojing and Guzhang: the core of the Tujia chieftaincy of Yongshun.

candidates.name: Yongshun
candidates.meaning: "Eternal obedience": the Yongshun garrison, prefecture (1729) and chieftaincy over the Tujia in the area.
candidates.fit: 38% of the region's people; the Yongshun prefecture (1729-1911) and Yongshun chieftaincy covered Baojing, Guzhang, Longshan and Sangzhi too.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; Laosicheng (the chieftains' seat) is a World Heritage site.

candidates.name: Xizhou
candidates.meaning: "Stream prefecture": Tang and Five Dynasties prefecture (691-939) seated at Laosicheng, home to the Xizhou bronze pillar treaty.
candidates.fit: Seat at Yongshun with territory over Baojing, Guzhang, Longshan and Sangzhi; fits the region better than one county.
candidates.recognisability: Zh-wiki 溪州 article exists but is mostly about a Taiwan town; 322 hits with 湖南, many about this prefecture.
candidates.source_note: 溪州，691-939，湖南永顺县驻地灵溪镇东老司城 (sources.md); "唐朝置溪州，宋朝为永顺州"

regions.notes: Xizhou may be confused with Xizhou in Taiwan (same spelling, different place only by context).

regions.summary: Yuanling, Jishou and Luxi where the You and Wu rivers meet the Yuan.

candidates.name: Yuanling
candidates.meaning: "Yuan mound": a Han county (202 BC) on the Yuan River, seat of Chen prefecture for centuries.
candidates.fit: 36% of the region's people; the region holds 62% of the county; the most central and historic part.

candidates.name: Jishou
candidates.meaning: City and seat of Xiangxi prefecture; meaning of the name not confirmed in the sources read.
candidates.fit: 32% of the region's people, 99% of the city held; prefecture capital of the Tujia and Miao area.
candidates.source_note: article listed in sources.md for region 5

candidates.name: Chenzhou
candidates.meaning: Sui prefecture (589) named for the Chen stream; covered Yuanling, Chenxi, Luxi and Xupu.
candidates.fit: Seated at Yuanling, covers Yuanling and Luxi, and also reaches Chenxi and Xupu (region 7).
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 675 hits with 湖南; spelled like Chenzhou (郴州) in Hunan, a different city.

regions.notes: Chenzhou may be read as Chenzhou (郴州, a different city in south Hunan).

regions.summary: Mayang, Fenghuang (Hunan) and Songtao (Guizhou) in the Miao hills.

candidates.name: Fenghuang
candidates.meaning: "Phoenix": a county named for the Phoenix Mountain; home to an ancient town on the Tuo River.
candidates.fit: 33% of the region's people, 93% of the county held; Fenghuang prefecture (1705-1911) seated here.
candidates.recognisability: Famous ancient town and Shen Congwen's home.
candidates.source_note: 凤凰厅 1705-1911, 湖南凤凰县凤凰城 (sources.md)

candidates.name: Mayang
candidates.meaning: Miao autonomous county; Mayang county since 620, on the Jin River.
candidates.fit: 34% of the region's people, 99% of the county held.
